newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambique begins first census in 17 years.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique begins first census in 17 years.

text.p: Mozambique, one of the world's poorest countries emerging from 16 years of civil war, began a census on Friday.
The census which will take two weeks is the most detailed held in the southern African country, seeking answers to 68 questions compared to 30 asked in the last census in 1980.

Mozambique is seriously short of statistical information, mainly because of war between 1976 and 1992. The 1980 census was possible only because of a break in the war between the government and Renamo rebels.
In addition to finding out how many people live in the country, the census is expected to provide data on a wide range of subjects such as housing and agriculture.

The census form also asks: "Where did you live when the war ended?" This will give the government an idea of how many people were refugees in neighbouring countries during the war and how many were internally displaced.
There are three key questions on language -- can you speak Portuguese, in what language did you learn to speak, and what language do you normally speak at home?

It is widely accepted that most Mozambicans speak to each other in their local African language though Portuguese is Mozambique's official language and lingua franca because Portugal was the former colonial power.
But there has been a lengthy debate in the press over whether Portuguese should be dumped in favour of English, the official language of all Mozambique's neighbouring countries.
The 1980 census found Mozambique's population at 12.1 million. Two calculations in recent years, based on separate methods, put the population in the mid-1990s at about 17.4 million.

One calculation was based on projections from the 1980 census, assuming an annual population growth rate of 2.6 percent. The other estimate was extrapolated from voter registration figures in the country's first multi-party elections in 1994.
If the projections are correct, the population of Mozambique in the year 2000 will be about 20 million.
